narrative:
The 2024 San Francisco Giants were a team perpetually caught between promise and disappointment, never quite finding the consistency needed to push into playoff contention. They opened the year with a .500 March and a losing April, the bullpen already flashing warning signs as Taylor Rogers and Camilo Doval struggled in high-leverage moments. Yet the offense showed flashes of life — Thairo Estrada's early double, Patrick Bailey's grand slam in May — that kept hope alive through the season's first two months.

May and June told a story of a team fighting hard but leaking runs at the worst times. The bullpen, particularly Doval and Tyler Rogers, repeatedly surrendered leads in crushing fashion. But the Giants still managed winning records in May and July, buoyed by clutch individual moments: Bailey's grand slam, Estrada's three-run homer against the Cubs, and Brett Wisely's game-winning single in early July. These heroics masked structural flaws — an offense that ranked among the league's weakest and relievers who couldn't hold late-game advantages.

August brought a brief resurgence, with Matt Chapman delivering the season's second-biggest positive swing with a clutch two-run double on August 30th, but Doval continued to be a liability, surrendering a three-run homer to Luis García Jr. that same week. September was where the Giants' playoff hopes finally expired. They went 12-13 in their final month, closing a season in which they scored and allowed nearly identical run totals — a coin-flip team that finished two games under .500.

Heliot Ramos provided one of the season's emotional high points with his 21st home run in mid-September, a glimpse of the young outfielder's future, but Anthony Santander's 42nd homer off Ryan Walker days later was a fitting coda to a campaign defined by near-misses. The Giants finished 80-82, their pitching and offense both hovering near league average without excelling at either, leaving fans to wonder what a healthier roster and a more reliable bullpen might have produced.

chapters.title: Early Struggles, Early Sparks
chapters.description: The Giants stumble through April with a losing record, though Estrada's clutch double offers a hint of the offense's potential.

chapters.title: May Madness: Slams and Surrenders
chapters.description: A winning May is defined by wild swings — Bailey's grand slam lifts the Giants while the bullpen repeatedly gives games away.

chapters.title: June's Heartbreaks and Heroes
chapters.description: The Giants go 12-15 in June, with Estrada's three-run blast providing the season's most electric moment amid a string of bullpen failures.

chapters.title: Winning Ugly in July
chapters.description: Despite high-leverage losses to Pittsburgh and Cleveland, the Giants gut out a 13-12 July on the back of clutch hits from Wisely and Yastrzemski.

chapters.title: August's False Dawn
chapters.description: Chapman's clutch double briefly reignites playoff hopes, but Doval's continued struggles and a losing September extinguish any remaining postseason dreams.

chapters.title: September Fade
chapters.description: Ramos's 21st homer offers a bright spot for the future, but the Giants close 12-13, finishing two games below .500 and out of the playoff picture.
